label: Archer Pavilion begun (finished 1711)
more: Henry Grey, who became Duke of Kent in 1710, commissioned Thomas Archer to design a banqueting house at the south end of the Long Water. It cost £1,809 and was built in 1709–1711. Hauduroy painted the interior in 1712.

label: Capability Brown at work (1758–1760)
more: Jemima, Marchioness Grey, and her husband Philip Yorke brought in Lancelot Brown. He joined the canals and made the straight boundary ones curve, but left the Duke of Kent's formal core alone. He was consulted again briefly in 1778 and 1779.

label: Bath House built (to 1771)
more: Edward Stevens built a cold plunge bath and dressing room for Jemima, styled as a ruined Roman bath in rough ironstone, with a cascade over the spring that fed it. Work was under way by September 1769 and nearly finished in May 1771.

label: Orangery; Earl becomes first RIBA President
more: Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey designed the Orangery for the orange trees he bought from King Louis-Philippe (dated about 1835 in the listing; 1838–1839 in a later Historic England report). He was also the first President of the Institute of British Architects, founded in 1834.

label: Bath House plunge bath filled in
more: Earl de Grey filled in the Bath House's bath, no longer needed after hot and cold baths were fitted in the old house in 1827–1828. The 1960s restoration dug it out and rebuilt it.
